Hypercasual TeardownGoing Balls · Mobile web
Speed is a resource. Space is the price.

Going
Balls

A rolling platformer turns one finger into a continuous negotiation between momentum and the edge.

The strongest adaptation preserves the player's ability to slow down, line up and commit. Its rewards should lead back to that decision quickly.

Pronetis / SupersonicPortrait, one fingerAnalysis · 06 Oct 2026

01
The product

Simple contact.
Many reasons to return.

Going Balls is a portrait, physics-led rolling platformer: a ball travels over suspended courses toward a finish, while the player adjusts speed and direction with swipes. Coins, ball appearances and world themes sit around that skill loop. Later play adds bonus tracks, special courses, competitive-looking races and short reward games. These layers broaden the occasion to play; they do not make the basic steering decision more complicated.

The two recordings show resumed accounts in different states: an earlier-looking Level 17–27 sequence with Epic levels, and a Level 51–59 sequence with Skip'its, races and additional reward screens. Together they show a family of evolving experiences, not a single verified current ruleset. The exact builds, a fresh-install tutorial and a final campaign boundary are unknown.

4.2 / 5Google Play US header: 983K reviews, 100M+ downloads; ads and in-app purchases. Snapshot: 06 Oct 2026. Listing
4.6 / 5UK App Store: about 61K ratings. Different audience and storefront; counts are not combined. Listing
No critic scoreMetacritic lists an iOS release on 19 Feb 2020, zero critic reviews and no Metascore. A focused Steam search found no matching official full-game or demo listing. Metacritic

A lineage of rolling games. Pronetis presents Going Balls as taking Gyrosphere Trials further and identifies Iron Ball Ride as an earlier step. Its own site reports more than 100 million downloads. This supports a continuing design lineage; it does not establish the team size, budget or today's chart rank. Pronetis

What reception tells us. Selected Play reviews praise a relaxing loop and later difficulty, while criticising interruption frequency and eventual course repetition. These are individual experiences. They suggest testing the ratio of rolling time to reward-menu time, and the difference between meaningful remixes and repeated scenery; they do not prove population-wide retention effects. Player reviews

A live product, not a frozen specimen. App Store notes include a ball-fall fix in 1.4.14, a critical loading fix in 1.4.24, improved ball-unlock UX in 1.4.33 and a Back to School season in 1.4.35. These changes inform boot, falling and unlock regression tests. They are not evidence that either recording uses those versions. Version history

02
The defining verb

Steer the ball.
Manage the commitment.

The challenge is not simply to move left or right before an obstacle. The player must preserve enough forward motion to cross a gap while limiting the motion that carries the ball past a turn, off a rail or through a landing. A straight approach invites acceleration; a constricted corner asks the player to spend that speed before changing direction.

Choice → consequence → next choice. Acceleration changes the distance covered before a correction takes effect. A jump commits the ball to an approach speed and alignment. Landing creates the next steering problem, often close to a rail, coin line or turn. Coins tempt the player to move off the safe centre, so collection is a route decision rather than a score counter disconnected from play.

One finger supplies both axes. The source's start instruction is an energetic invitation to swipe; it is not a calibration guide. The official description explicitly gives the player control of speed and direction. A web adaptation that automatically runs forward at one fixed speed would discard a defining decision. Official control description

Feel that matters: legible inertia, continuous course geometry, a visible landing destination and a quick return after a mistake. Exact acceleration, drag gain, friction and airborne steering are design space rather than measured source constants.

Analytical model · qualitative, not measured physics

The momentum corridor

Success occupies a moving window: enough speed to reach the landing, enough control to stay on it.

Align

Slow on a wide section. Centre the ball before a narrow rail or turn. Lower speed gives corrections more time.

Commit

Build speed on the approach. A ramp or booster changes the cost of braking and the reachable landing.

Recover

Reduce drift after contact. Overspeed turns a safe arrival into a new edge hazard.

More time to correctUseful jump momentumLess landing margin

Interpretation of the course affordances, supported by the rail and exposed-corner figures. It describes the adaptation's tuning problem; it is not a graph of the original engine's numeric response.

Read the next section→Choose speed + line→Commit through hazard→Land / fall→Correct / retry
03
The obstacle grammar

Geometry teaches.
Combinations examine.

Wide wooden tracks establish a safe centre. The level then removes space, changes elevation or moves the surface under the ball. Green chevrons distinguish an acceleration aid; rails and yellow-black markings communicate a constrained, hazardous passage. A ring of coins can make the risky route attractive without requiring another instruction.

The useful unit for rebuilding is a readable situation, not a prop checklist: a safe approach, a visible threat, an opportunity to adjust, an irreversible commitment and a landing from which the player can recover. A propeller next to a blind corner is a different problem from the same propeller on a wide platform.

Rails / ramps / gapsAlign, build momentum, then commit.Longer gaps, smaller landings, a turn after landing.Paired rails; ramp/jump behaviour described in both recordings
Moving or rotating surfacesEnter at a useful phase and leave toward the exit.Combine timing with narrow entry/exit routes.Circular platform; movement reported, period unmeasured
Disappearing cellsContinue rather than hesitate on spent ground.Route planning competes with the pressure to keep moving.Hex track; collapse timing remains report-level

Failure should identify the next correction

The source exposes a familiar fall-and-return structure and a separate Revive / Skip decision in later special play. A bounded inspection of the earlier video shows the football falling off the track and subsequently returning to the approach. It confirms that the episode continues; it does not establish unlimited lives, a global checkpoint rule or the exact reset velocity.

A retry becomes productive when the player can name the mistake: entered the rail off-centre, carried too much lateral momentum, reached a moving platform at the wrong phase. A long monetisation choice inserted here competes with that short-lived memory. In the web design, return to a known safe anchor and keep the same obstacle phase readable.

04
Resources and interruption

A small verb.
A large reward surface.

Coins and cosmetic selection turn successful courses into visible account change. Keys convert collection into a chest-opening choice. The later recording adds pink Skip'its and blue checkered race tickets; they have different roles and should never be merged into one generic currency. These resources connect otherwise separate screens.

Skip'its explicitly exchange an ad watch for an immediate reward. The reward structure is therefore part of the pacing structure: the player's choice to keep rolling is repeatedly compared with a larger immediate payout. The web version can preserve rewards and anticipation while removing that payment for continuation.

A consequential reward transition

A displayed 99,999 chest payout is followed by a balance increase of 199,998 and the loss of one pink ticket. That pair is consistent with the x2 claim. It makes the trade tangible, but the extreme value is an episode-specific jackpot, not a sensible default web economy.

Cosmetics broaden identity, not the control model

The ball catalogue includes familiar material, food and novelty shapes. World previews offer a separate environment selection. The observed prices are visible choices, not verified purchase deductions. There is no delivered evidence that a Tomato, Cat or Football changes the physics; the web adaptation should keep identical collision and handling across all appearances.

05
A portfolio around the ball

The same object,
a different reason to move.

Main-course progression is interrupted by offers that change the task, the reward cadence or both. The ball remains a familiar avatar, so the player can enter a new situation with little identity cost. The source's special modes should be analysed individually; a menu label does not prove a complete ruleset.

The long-term tension

New tracks and worlds create anticipation; expensive ball appearances give ordinary coin pickups a future purpose. But a large reward can finish a collection goal faster than ordinary play, while repeated menus can make a short track feel like an interstitial between offers. A web adaptation should maintain a visible next course, a reachable next appearance and optional side modes, with no compulsory reward-game chain before rolling again.

06
Art and feedback

A toy world that
stays readable in motion.

Wood under the ball. Cool space beyond it. A small number of saturated signals for things that change the run.

Keep the material hierarchy

Warm tracks separate the traversable surface from the cyan void. Green acceleration marks, purple breakables and yellow-black edge warnings can remain recognisable without reproducing commercial character skins or a branded world. A restrained ball shadow is more useful than a dense particle trail when the player must judge contact.

Let the camera prepare the next action

The player should see the intended landing before leaving the ramp, and the next turn before touching the narrow section. Follow position with speed-dependent look-ahead, anticipate course yaw gradually and avoid remapping a held drag during a camera turn. Fading decorative occluders is a separate improvement; it cannot repair a confusing control frame.

Use rewards as punctuation

A coin pickup can brighten the counter and emit a short chime. Checkpoint contact should change the anchor marker once, and a finish should briefly open the visual rhythm with an arch, confetti and a clear Continue action. Reward reveals may be colourful, but must allow the player to leave them and resume the course loop.

Sound should explain, then embellish

Use a quiet looping music bed, speed-aware rolling texture, distinct pickup, boost, impact, fall, checkpoint and finish sounds. Original audio fidelity has not been verified. This is an original sound direction to be implemented and listened to; it is not a claim that the source soundtrack has been heard.

A tested donor signal, a new application

Designed transfer The archived Hole.io report's “The city gets out of the way” section and R06 document buildings turning transparent when they obscure the hole. Its embedded fig-xray was opened and checked. The source frame shows foreground structures faded while the controlled object remains readable.

For Going Balls, fade only decorative objects that obstruct the ball, approach or landing. Keep contact geometry and moving hazards opaque, with a silhouette outline if needed. Exclude Hole.io's growth, swallowing, city destruction and timer systems. The expected benefit is fewer hidden-path corrections; verify it in actual phone motion, including a thumb over the lower screen.

Donor: archived Hypercasual Teardown — Hole.io — EN.html, “The city gets out of the way”, R06 / fig-xray; source video 4fcy6T6ku6A, 108.1 s, 2021 recording. This is a cross-game visual signal, not observed Going Balls behaviour.

Complete-game handoff · mobile web · bug.games

Build layer

A complete free rolling game, ready to specify with named fidelity limits. No game has been built or published as part of this teardown.

Observed means an inspected frame or bounded player sequence supports that state. Inferred connects observed states without proving every intermediate action. Designed defines the new game's requirements. Reported-only details remain explicit design space. Source versions are unknown and must not be merged into a universal rule.

Scope and non-negotiable decisions

Control speed as well as direction

C1. The player chooses an approach speed and line under a gap, rail or turning constraint; that choice changes the reachable landing and the available correction after contact. A fixed-speed auto-runner fails this core test.

Make falling informative

C2. The player recognises which alignment or timing choice caused the fall, returns to a safe anchor quickly and can try a changed approach. A retry must preserve learning rather than require a currency purchase.

Make collection compete with safety

C3. A coin line offers a detour or a less forgiving alignment; securing the reward changes the next cosmetic goal. Cosmetic choice must leave the physical performance unchanged.

Let optional modes change the task

C4. The player accepts a race, arena or harder course to change the objective, resolves it, and returns to the persistent track ladder. Side play cannot erase the current course or become compulsory.

Complete target structure

D01 · Designed delivery boundary. Deliver the whole game below as one portable playable HTML with bundled assets and a conditional platform boundary. A working control scene, an initial chapter or a menu of unavailable modes is not the deliverable. Suggested implementation order may start with controls, but must end with the full connected product.

The content budget below is a concrete baseline for a complete adaptation, not a claimed source count. The builder may reshape counts and pacing through playtesting while retaining every listed system, a substantial authored course sequence, a completed collection and repeatable post-sequence play. All designs and changed budgets must be recorded in its own working notes.

Progression and economy decisions

D02. The main ladder unlocks course families; skill gates use completion rather than a purchase. Coins come from collected objects, clears and optional mode results and buy cosmetic balls / world palettes. Keys connect milestone clears to chest choices. Skip’its, ticket-gated race entry and server weekly rank are omitted from the target economy. The free game contains every course family and mode; a cosmetic purchase never buys grip, speed, a wider collider or checkpoint access.

Illustrative tuning, not a source rule: start at 100 coins per standard clear plus collected coins, with an entry-level cosmetic around 400–600 and later appearances 1,500–3,000. A key every third clear is a starting cadence. Simulate the first 20 minutes, adjust costs to create an early reachable goal, and log the adopted values. A large optional award must not flatten the whole collection. Use seeded draws and transaction IDs so reload cannot grant the same reveal twice.

D03. Bronze is completion; silver is a limited-fall or route target; gold is a clean run with a stated time/collection objective. The builder chooses per-course thresholds after timed play. Post-ladder remixes vary already validated modules and phase relationships, with reachable landings and a capped difficulty profile. Repetition is advertised as mastery, not as an endless stream of invented unique levels.

Settings belong to the target game

D04 · Designed. Put a Settings entry on the hub and pause panel. Provide a complete EN / RU interface switch, separate Music volume and Sound effects volume sliders from 0–100%, and optional sensitivity. Persist preferences device-locally under a separate settings key. Translate buttons, objectives, prices, result text, tutorials, errors, local-AI labels and purchase states; do not translate only the top menu. Audio gain is platform master mute × that channel's slider. A platform unmute must not undo a player-set zero. The teardown remains English; these controls are requirements for the game to be built.

No quota filled by a vaguely similar genre.Do not introduce click-to-grow, training, shared survival or social loops without new evidence and a relevant player problem.

Confidence is secondary knowledge-page evidence. The Backflip FTUE and Tower of Hell sections were read; there is no direct donor playtest or claim of transfer performance.

Normal first session~30 seconds~2 minutes~5 minutes~10 minutes~20 minutes
Player does / sees / next pullFirst drag, speed change and one checkpoint; cue disappears after success. Next: visible exit.First clear, one settlement and immediate next course; knows falling returns to an anchor.A narrower rail or turn combines speed with alignment; first cosmetic goal reachable.First family mastery beat; optional bonus/challenge, decline works; collection preview explains cost.Several families / modes encountered without debug access; earned cosmetic used; next course and mastery pull remain visible.

Designed evaluation: walk the first 20 minutes on an ordinary phone with one hand, both sound on and sound off. Record actual milestones rather than treating the table as evidence that the built game already achieves them. Adjust pacing without adding daily login, server competition or a parallel training economy.

bug.games runtime boundary

D05 · Designed integration, SDK reference checked 06 Oct 2026. The game must be playable standalone, including file://, with no platform service. Bundle the renderer, level data and media into the portable HTML. When embedded, conditionally load the platform module from /sdk/bloomplay.js and initialise it. An absent SDK and a rejected/timed-out init are different conditions; either should leave the free game playable with an honest local-only save state.

  • Call loaded() once the playable UI is interactive. Use loading/failed messages only for real boot progress or an actual unrecoverable rendering failure.
  • Call gameplayStart() / gameplayStop() at real play boundaries: first control, pause, result, mode change and exit. They are not animation-frame events. Handle repeated calls idempotently.
  • Handle onPause for hidden, sign-in, purchase, dialog and page interruptions. Suspend simulation, clocks and voices, clear held input and flush committed progress. onResume must respect a user pause.
  • Platform mute silences both audio channels without pausing physics. Apply master mute with each saved Music / SFX setting; a later unmute retains a user's zero channel.
  • Use the SDK save layer for embedded progress, e.g. bloomplay.save({key: 'save', cache: 'roll.save.v1'}), and await readiness before replacing or resetting data. Cache locally for offline play; preserve coins, grants and unlock transactions. Settings remain device-local in their own key.
  • A failed account read is not an empty account. With a manual fallback, only a successful read with version 0 means empty. Never overwrite a good account save because a read rejected. Show local-only / sync-unavailable status at the save boundary.
  • Report exact declared progress.moment(name) labels once at meaningful progress. Do not duplicate automatic bp_pageview or automatic gameplay session analytics.

The base game is solo. Local AI and a personal best board require no room, presence, shared board or server simulation. No camera or microphone permissions are needed.

Analytics that answer this game's questions

Use bloomplay.analytics.track for the events below. Generate an ephemeral session ID and bounded run/transaction IDs; send no direct personal identifiers, raw pointer traces or high-frequency telemetry. Keep properties categorical or rounded. When offline, analytics failure cannot block play or reward settlement.

Game eventExact triggerNecessary propertiesQuestion
roll_first_controlFirst input changes the ball’s velocity after Ready.input_kind, tutorial_variant, seconds_to_control, localeDoes the initial cue produce useful motion?
roll_checkpointBall enters a new checkpoint trigger, once per run and anchor.course_id, family, anchor_index, elapsed_sWhere does progress stall?
roll_fallA supported ball loses the route and crosses the fall boundary; one event until recovery.course_id, module_id, mode, anchor_index, speed_band, cause_categoryIs a specific landing / turn unreadable or mistuned?
roll_retryA fall recovery becomes controllable at the anchor.course_id, falls_this_run, recovery_ms, chosen_restart_kindDoes the player re-enter quickly, and choose a whole-course restart?
roll_clearFinish is validated and reward committed, once per run.course_id, family, elapsed_s, falls, pickups, medalWhich course combination is challenging without being opaque?
roll_mode_choicePlayer accepts or declines a side-mode offer.offer_id, mode, decision, ladder_courseDo alternatives appeal without trapping continuation?
roll_mode_resultRace / arena / Goal Ball / portal resolves and settlement commits.mode, content_id, elapsed_s, outcome, reward_coinsDoes the changed task resolve, and does its reward dominate?
roll_cosmetic_unlockCommitted base-game coin transaction grants a new appearance.item_id, coin_cost, balance_after, progress_familyHow long until a usable collection goal?
roll_reward_choicePlayer collects, skips animation or declines an optional reward play.reward_kind, choice, committed_coins, seconds_on_screenHow much session time is spent outside rolling?
roll_settingsPlayer commits a changed setting on release / select, not every slider frame.locale, music_band, sfx_band, setting_changedAre independent audio and complete translations used?
roll_save_statusSave boundary changes healthy ↔ local-only / read failed.origin, failure_kind, pending_changesAre repeat sessions losing progress or hiding sync failure?

Later optional product analytics belong to the actual purchase flow only. Use an intent/result event with product ID and result code; do not log a success on opening a preview, or duplicate a platform event when the SDK already reports it.

Show sale only from SDK-approved getProducts() catalogue; displayed price comes from the SDK.

D06 · If an extra is later implemented: call platform getProducts() and getEntitlements(); availability comes from the catalogue and ownership from a successful entitlement read / confirmed purchase. An empty catalogue does not reveal why an item is unavailable. Hide sale controls when unavailable; keep a previously owned durable cosmetic usable if withdrawn. A failed entitlement read must not revoke cached confirmed ownership. Pending, cancelled, insufficient-coins and failed purchases grant nothing; confirmed success grants exactly once. Never spend the game's earned cosmetic coins as if they were platform coins. A platform purchase modal pauses the run safely. Implement mock success/cancel/error/insufficient paths before asking for product review.

Acceptance cases for the later build

These are expected tests, not results of an implementation. Source-based expectations and Designed choices are identified above; the builder records real outcomes after play.

  1. T01 · C1 / B07: A fresh player in 390×844 portrait drags with one thumb, sees the ball accelerate and reaches the first checkpoint; cue stops only after actual success.
  2. T02 · C1: Same gap, low versus useful approach speed. Insufficient momentum misses; sufficient aligned motion lands. Braking changes the result.
  3. T03 · C1 / C3: Same rail at two alignments and speeds. Off-centre entry falls; a corrected line stays supported; coin detour has a visible cost.
  4. T04 · C2 / D01: Fall → cause visible → cleared input → neutral safe-anchor reset → changed second approach. Free repeat works; clean-run medal can still be lost.
  5. T05: Booster followed by landing/turn: speed increase is visible, upcoming surface readable and excess speed recoverable through braking.
  6. T06: Moving platform and propeller: the player can wait for a different phase. Pause freezes both obstacle and ball phase.
  7. T07: Cell touched → readable warning → support lost after Designed delay. Retry restores a learnable layout and phase.
  8. T08: Fast finish crossing commits once even between frames; no tunnelling or finish-to-void softlock. Reward equals the stated result.
  9. T09 · R10 / D02: Bonus count displayed before settlement, collection commits once, reload does not duplicate it; decline advances immediately.
  10. T10: Precision challenge allows free anchor retry or voluntary full restart; leaving preserves main-ladder progress.
  11. T11: All three portal worlds work with the same controls; no decorative occlusion hides a required landing.
  12. T12: Local AI race begins after countdown, resolves placement, grants its defined reward once; local label is visible and PB persists.
  13. T13: Banana arena explains timer and score, resolves ties consistently, stops collection at result and returns to saved ladder.
  14. T14: Goal Ball resets after each goal, resolves at Designed third goal, handles stalemate without invisible advantage and can be exited.
  15. T15: Wheel, slot and pegboard each have working revealed outcomes, stated pools, skippable animation and no repeated reward on reload.
  16. T16 · C3: Insufficient coins prevent unlock without deduction; affordable unlock grants once; all skins match radius / handling; saved selection appears next run.
  17. T17: Key chest cannot spend a nonexistent key, choose an opened box or repeat a grant; overflow policy and exhausted-board reset are explicit.
  18. T18: Authored ladder ends in a clear completion state; mastery/replay/remixes remain playable. A sampled remix has reachable landing and a real exit.
  19. T19 · D04: Switch EN→RU→EN in hub, gameplay, result and error screens. Every player string translates, longer labels fit and Settings persists after reload.
  20. T20 · D04: Music 0 / SFX 100 and Music 100 / SFX 0 independently work; both 0 is silent; platform mute/unmute preserves both choices; listen to the actual final assets.
  21. T21: Pointer cancel, phone rotation, tab hide and SDK modal clear input and pause. Resume does not cancel user pause or accumulate offscreen physics time.
  22. T22: Standalone file and SDK absent / init rejected remain playable; storage unavailable shows honest session-only state. Reload with working storage restores committed progress.
  23. T23: Account read failure cannot overwrite remote save or remove confirmed ownership. Valid empty/version-0 state can adopt local progress; settings never merge with medals.
  24. T24: Normal 20-minute phone play reaches the hooks milestones without debug shortcuts; also play muted and repeat after reload. Capture actual pace and next-goal understanding.
  25. T25 · donor signal: Same canyon corner with decorative opacity versus fading. Ball and landing are readable in motion; rails, bat and other contact geometry stay visible.
  26. T26 · platform: Loaded, gameplay boundaries and declared moments fire once at their real states; no repeated automatic pageview/session events. Offline analytics error affects no reward.
  27. T27 · optional extras: With products empty, no empty shop. If later built, mock pending/cancel/error/insufficient/success; no grant except confirmed success, no double grant, withdrawn owned item stays usable.
  28. T28 · whole product: Every inventory row is reachable and resolves, all production assets are bundled and licensed, and the portable HTML works without the development folder or network.

Evidence, coverage and limits

Selected run: 2026-10-06T09-00-45-693Z-def136f4 only. START-HERE, packet manifests, both frozen Authoring skills, two complete raw Gemini reports, both exact request files and all 38 supplied captures were reviewed. Integrity checks verified 87 declared files with no hash failure. READY was treated as delivery status, not rule acceptance. No Gemini rerun occurred.

Source recordings. V1 · The HARDEST SECRET LEVELS In Going Balls! and V2 · Unlocking SECRET Levels In Going Balls, Kindly Keyin. Account state and level ranges are visible; exact release/build and first-install state are unavailable. Frame mappings below use recorded actual capture time, not requested descriptions. Phone-area crops retain the relevant UI; source file hashes remain in the index.

Autonomous completion. A bounded V2 171–195 s video fetch failed: first network resolution, then a 180-second helper timeout. The method was changed to the available YouTube browser player. Paused images at 188.30 and 193.30 s showed fall then return. No decoded source clip was obtained, so that transition is documented as browser observation rather than embedded motion proof. Original audio was not listened to with a verified audio-capable path. Movement periods, skin physics and complete mode rules remain Design space.

Semantic coverage. All captures were checked as shows / partial / not-shown against the actual pixels. Two facecam-only frames were excluded; shop frames establish pre-unlock prices rather than deductions. Named pig reward, precise collapse delay, the reported finish overshoot and camera-caused fall are not asserted as inspected facts. These limits do not prevent a complete target design, but they prevent a claim of exact source fidelity.

Short prompt for the receiving builder

Build this complete game

Build a complete portrait mobile web adaptation of Going Balls as one portable HTML, using this file’s Build layer and embedded figures. Preserve two-axis one-finger rolling: control speed, brake, align on narrow rails, commit to gaps and recover at free safe anchors. Deliver the full authored ladder across six obstacle families, bonus tracks, precision challenges, three portal worlds, local-AI races, Banana collection arenas, Goal Ball courts, optional wheel/slot/pegboard reward play, key chests, the complete cosmetic collection and post-ladder mastery/remixes. Keep cosmetic physics identical and all base content free. Use the confirmed source states as evidence, design unmeasured physics/mode details openly, and test decisions through normal phone play. Give the game warm toy-like tracks, readable cool voids, clear hazards, anticipatory camera, faded decorative occluders and finished original/licensed music and SFX. Include full EN/RU, separate Music/SFX sliders and device-local settings. Follow the conditional bug.games SDK, save, analytics and moments plan; products remain empty unless a complete optional extra is later made review-ready. Verify all acceptance cases, including standalone/offline, pause/reload and the first 20 minutes; do not deliver a demo or a partial chapter.

Specification readiness: ready with named source-fidelity limits. Package: one self-contained illustrated HTML. Implementation/publication: future work; actual touch, rendering performance, audio mix, source asset licences and platform review remain to be tested during the build.
